complaint_what_happened:
I just received a notice in the mail ( XXXX-17 ) that my Chase credit card 's terms are changing. Specifically my interest rate is being increased from a moderate, but not entirely unreasonable ~10.9 % APR to 15.75 % APR. They did not provide what I consider to be a valid reason for the change. This was not based upon missing payments, nor upon credit history, or any other of what I would consider to be " reasonable '' justifications. 

Their sole justification effectively boiled down to " we 're not charging you a high enough interest rate, so we 're increasing your rate by ~50 %. '' In the more 'legalese ' verbiage of the notice, the only justification for this outrageous increase is " ... because your APRs are below the lowest APRs we currently offer on similar accounts. '' To me, this is simply them saying, " we 're not over-charging you to the same extent we 've managed to over-charge everyone else through our methodical long-term upward APR creep, so, we 're simply adding an extra 50 % to your APR, welcome to the club. '' Sure, they say that you can " reject the change, '' but if you do so, the only recourse listed is to " notify them in writing and then stop using and close the account. '' To me this is quite unacceptable. I 've had this account for years. Probably a decade even. They inherited it from Washington Mutual. And, up until now, they have never seemingly had a single problem with my account resting at 10 %, and taking their pound of flesh, so-to-speak. So, why, all of a sudden is a rate closer to what I would call a " penalty interest rate '' apparently the " lowest they 're willing to go ''? 

In my opinion, an un-telegraphed 50 % increase in APR, with no justification other than " we want more money, '' is simply nonsensical. 

And, for reference, my card at a competing " too big to fail '' institution is only 8.90 %, and has been equally stable for approximately a decade. Chase has always charged a higher rate with a lower spending cap than the equivalent larger cap and lower interest rate. Now, they seem intent to charge DOUBLE what I 'm paying at the other institution. To me that says, it 's not me that 's the problem, it 's them. Pure and simple.
